Badly designed puzzle game. Much of it is just trial and error. It develop general principles on such drawings. For instance, how radius proportion or frequency affects say the number of main humps or something to that effect. The position placement tool being imprecise also contributes to this. It'd be better if, for instance, you could create a precise subdivision at different radius. Even with the right solution its just trial and error to get it just right. Granted, programming something to 'check' the shape here is probably very hard, but it still doesn't make for a good puzzle game. For anyone playing, I personally found the latter half of the first chapters levels much harder than anything.

Did you ever play with spirograph as a kid? Not just the circle in a circle, but the reeeeeally insane stuff like the long bars that were just impossible to keep in position? 

Engare is that but you have to start with part of the final drawing and figure out where to put your pen. 

And I'm pretty sure you couldn't make half of this stuff with a sane spirograph set. 

This is genuinely one of the most unique puzzle games I've come across and it is gorgeous. The Arabic art references drive home that this isn't just a silly children's toy, But a stylization of a legitimate artistic and architectural tool that can help make real and beautiful things. 

It's also mind bending if you're not used to thinking about how nested rotations can behave. 

Everyone who has even a passing interest in art, puzzles, or geometry genuinely needs to try this.

What a beautiful and amazing experience. If you are interested in design and geometric patterns, then this is a wonderful game. Many patterns are showcased visually, and the Islamic Art Tools sandbox is worth the price alone.

Does it do what it says on the tin? I suppose it does. But I expected more from it.

Instead of enjoying the shapes, I was frustrated by the way I interacted with the sliders and how I kept having to re-click my dot. (Also, minor early-game annoyance.. I hadn't realized the example path was drawn with dashes, so I was utterly confused on that really early puzzle with the domino effect on how to create a non-contiguous line, which made me focus on the wrong part of the puzzle for like 20+ minutes because I utterly over-estimated the ambition of the puzzle...)

Instead of enjoying creativity, I found myself annoyed that many of the levels were immensely similar and that it was just a fiddly try-and-repeat until I got the sliders where I wanted them to.

I had hoped to walk away from this with some real insights into the patterns. And perhaps I can still get that to some degree from the creative editor section. But instead of happy feelings about the way the game enlightened me on a fresh new path of understanding, I instead feel myself lost going 'that's cool, I guess'.

It would be a far stronger game if it were able to feed into the proverbial 'eureka' by means of great puzzle design and level progression, but for me it never got anywhere close to that.

Maybe putting more creativity into the hands of the player could have helped. For example: create a shape of 49 roughly equally sized partitions. Or something with double the amount of triangle-like shapes than squarish ones. Create something with no concave shapes. Etc. Or letting a player put down multiple dots with different colors, which need to pleasingly interact visually. Etc.

Depending on what you are looking for, you may enjoy this game a lot more than I did.

Look at the screenshots. Do all the shapes appeal to you? Is this game's price justified for one or two hours of interesting shapes for you? I got it on sale, I think I got a fair value.

The puzzles are fine, but it's the implementation I like. It's a buttery smooth piece of software that does these loopy shapes. Some you might recognize from calculus or from seeing in Persian or Islamic art, and some are just nice loopy shapes. The nice thing here is that you get to see them in motion, you see what kind of movement these shapes emerge from, and the fact that it's a smooth render on your machine and not a video makes everything look so nice and clean. Again, drawing shapes on a computer is nothing new, it's how the concept is presented that makes it all work.

As a puzzler, it's not the most challenging, but as an experience, it is really novel. I really agree with the one blurb about grinning from ear to ear when it clicks on some levels.

The nice thing here as well is that it does not rely on typical gaming tropes, which leads me to think I can sit just about anyone in front of a screen, not people who are already into games, and have them enjoy this (if not beat all the levels in one to three hours)

I've had my eye on this (as in been in my wishlist) for years under the presumption that it was little more than a rudimentary editing/modelling tool. Well I finally had the chance to pick this up and give it a try. Two and a half dollars (on sale) and a little over 80 minutes later I can say this game needs more attention towards it.

Ever played The Incredible Machine series or it's spiritual successor Contraption Maker? Well this is that but geometry instead of trying to make rube goldberg machines, which is more fun and satisfying than it sounds. In the levels you are given rudimentary devices that you need to place a dot on, once you place the dot on the device it leaves a line as it's dragged along the screen and you need to experiment to try and make specific shapes to beat the level.

You know how with those games you only really get satisfaction if you either make the rube goldberg machine correctly or something funny happens? Well nearly every time you attempt a puzzle in Engare whether you are right or wrong is a treat as your attempt at a puzzle still will begin to create a beautifully satisfying shape; in fact one of my few complaints of this game is that for a decent amount of the levels the line trails being left by the dot don't go on for very long with incorrect answers; it would've been nice to have an option to let it keep going so we can see what beautiful shapes our incorrect answers create.

In fact, let's get the minor cons out of the way real quick. The music is good but I feel the variety available to you in this game could get grating if you for some reason play this nonstop for over two hours at once. It's nowhere near Animal Crossing: New Horizons levels of grating that is the first week or so of a new game (where you spend said entire week or so stuck with only one single music track), but for me as someone who enjoyed the music at the very least I noticed that it might get old if I played this game for an absurd amount of time at once.

The only other real con is that depending on the level the game can either be very forgiving or very nit-picky. I'll have to use very rudimentary symbol based examples to explain this. Let's say a mission requires you to make a /v\ line to beat it; sometimes you can get away with finding the solution but adding the dot too early resulting in a \/v\ line which the game accepts that you did it. Sometimes it doesn't but will give you it if you were too late and the line was v\. Sometimes it gives you no room for error and you need to be pretty much exact. I feel the game would be too easy if every level had universal rules to be very generous with timing but I feel my previous suggestion of letting a wrong answer line keep going so you can at least see if you were too early or too late for the next attempt would fix this, enough so that with a feature like this I wouldn't mind the game giving you no room for error across all levels.

Aside from those small cons this game is amazing for what it is, and at seemingly anytime you can use the "creator" mode of this game and proceed to go wild with making very beautiful patterns and shapes in both 2D and 3D. From parts of stylized buildings to stained glass windows to shapes to spice up patterns to go on any kind of item, I can see many uses for the editor mode.

Definitely pick this up if you enjoy games like Incredible Machine/Contraption Maker, want a chill game or want a fun editing tool for making patterns. Nowadays has a sequel and unlike Engare that took a long time for me to finally give it a try, I feel it's sequel Tandis will be in my library a heck of a lot sooner.
